regimens.indication: Life-Threatening Recurrent Ventricular Fibrillation or Hemodynamically Unstable Ventricular Tachycardia - Loading Regimen (Adults)

refs.quote: Pacerone is indicated for the treatment of documented, life-threatening recurrent ventricular fibrillation and life-threatening recurrent hemodynamically unstable tachycardia in adults who have not responded to adequate doses of other available antiarrhythmics or when alternative agents cannot be tolerated.

Initiate treatment with a loading dose of 800 to 1600 mg/day until initial therapeutic response occurs (usually 1 to 3 weeks). Once adequate arrhythmia control is achieved, or if side effects become prominent, reduce Pacerone tablets dose to 600 to 800 mg/day for one month and then to the maintenance dose, usually 400 mg/day.

dose.frequency: daily (divided doses with meals for >=1000 mg/day) for 1-3 weeks, then 600-800 mg/day for 1 month

regimens.dose_text: Initiate in hospital/specialist setting with continuous ECG and resuscitation available. Loading dose: 800 to 1600 mg/day until initial response (usually 1-3 weeks), then 600 to 800 mg/day for 1 month before tapering to maintenance. Divide doses with meals if >= 1000 mg/day or GI intolerance.

hepatic.value: Boxed Warning for potentially fatal hepatotoxicity; obtain baseline and periodic liver transaminases and discontinue or reduce dose if transaminases exceed 3x normal or double in a patient with an elevated baseline. In cirrhotic patients, lower Cmax/average DEA levels are seen while mean amiodarone levels are unchanged.

refs.quote: Pacerone can cause hepatoxicity, which can be fatal. Obtain baseline and periodic liver transaminases and discontinue or reduce dose if the increase exceeds three times normal, or doubles in a patient with an elevated baseline. Discontinue Pacerone if the patient experiences signs or symptoms of clinical liver injury

mechanism_of_action.value: Amiodarone is a class III antiarrhythmic with electrophysiologic characteristics of all four Vaughan Williams classes: it lengthens cardiac action potential and refractoriness (class III), blocks sodium channels (class I), exerts noncompetitive antisympathetic action (class II), and slows SA/AV nodal conduction (class IV).

refs.quote: Amiodarone is considered a class III antiarrhythmic drug, but it possesses electrophysiologic characteristics of all four Vaughan Williams classes.
Amiodarone inhibits P-glycoprotein and CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2D6, and CYP3A, increasing exposure to other drugs.
These electrophysiologic effects are reflected in a decreased sinus rate of 15% to 20%, increased PR and QT intervals of about 10%, the development of U-waves, and changes in T-wave contour.

Because of amiodarone's long half-life, expect drug interactions to persist for weeks to months after discontinuation of amiodarone.

Available data from post-marketing reports and published case series indicate that amiodarone use in pregnant women may increase the risk for fetal adverse effects including neonatal hypo- and hyperthyroidism, neonatal bradycardia, neurodevelopmental abnormalities, preterm birth and fetal growth restriction.

tier.note: 5-axis synthesis: Post-marketing reports and case series show significant fetal toxicity (neonatal hypo/hyperthyroidism, bradycardia, QT prolongation, neurodevelopmental abnormalities, IUGR, preterm birth); animal studies show >90% abortions in rabbits at 2.7x MRHD and fetal toxicity in mice/rats below MRHD; reserve only for refractory life-threatening maternal arrhythmias.

pregnancy_pk.value: Breakthrough arrhythmias may occur during pregnancy as therapeutic treatment levels may be difficult to maintain due to increased volume of distribution and increased drug metabolism.

refs.quote: Breakthrough arrhythmias may also occur during pregnancy, as therapeutic treatment levels may be difficult to maintain due to the increased volume of distribution and increased drug metabolism inherent in the pregnant state.
Amiodarone and one of its major metabolites, DEA, are present in breastmilk at between 3.5% and 45% of the maternal weight-adjusted dosage of amiodarone.

lactation_summary.value: Amiodarone and DEA are present in breastmilk at 3.5% to 45% of the maternal weight-adjusted dose; cases of hypothyroidism and bradycardia in breastfed infants have been reported. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment.

refs.quote: There are cases of hypothyroidism and bradycardia in breastfed infants, although it is unclear if these effects are due to amiodarone exposure in breastmilk. Breastfeeding is not recommended during treatment with Pacerone
